correctness.rationale: Use Acosta-Portilla Theorem 4.6: two equivalent real norms share an intrinsic part iff their triangular defects are uniformly two-sided comparable. For 1<p<2 weighted-least-squares Hessian and finite-dimensional norm comparison give D2F_p >= c_{p,n} D2||.||2 with c=(p-1)n^{-(p-1)(1/p-1/2)}. For p>2 the reverse bound D2F_p <= C_{p,n} D2||.||2 with C=(p-1)n^{(p-1)(1/2-1/p)}. Continuity through coordinate hyperplanes and homogeneous line checks at origin make F_p-cE convex below 2 and CE-F_p convex above 2, yielding uniform defect comparisons. The small-angle pair x=e1,y=e1+t e2 has Delta_p=(1-2^(1-p))|t|^p/p+O(t^{2p}) and Delta_E=t^2/4+O(t4). These powers classify every (p,a) in the three stated classes: p=q<2 any a,b; p=q>2 with a=b=0; and all p>=2 with p=2 or a>0. For fixed p>2 and 0<a<b, Delta_b/Delta_a=(u+b)/(u+a) where u=Delta_p/Delta_E and u->0 near axis, so sharp maximum b/a; comparison m >=1 and <=(1+b)/(1+a) proves metric lower/upper logarithmic bounds and asymptotic coefficient one. Independent algebraic small-angle and source constant checks examined; sampled numerical checker is not universal proof.
residual_risks: Exhaustive finite certificates prove only finite objects; the analytic claims require their independently reconstructed universal proofs.

originality.rationale: Acosta-Portilla September 2026 full source introduces the intrinsic cone and proves exactly the general defect comparison criterion and metric formula; its l2-vs-l4 example separates unregularized norms but does not classify two-parameter additive p-plus-Euclidean mixtures or their logarithmic boundary law. A full polyhedral related result treats piecewise-linear norms, which differ from smooth mixed lp; a full Hilbertian result treats quadratic-inner-product norms and similarly does not subsume the mixed non-Hilbert case. Structured result is a new complete smooth family classification conditional on original source criterion, not a repackaging of Example 4.8.
residual_risks: Relatively recent intrinsic geometry literature might include a more general norm-curvature classification that implies these cases; no such covering theorem was identified.

The 2-parameter smooth strictly convex family is natural, and its full phase boundary at p=2 plus logarithmic blow-up of intrinsic distance to ordinary-norm convergence is a structural mechanism with clear meaning for norm geometry. The fact is not mechanically implied by the general part criterion without the substantive Hessian and asymptotic comparison.

limitations: Real finite-dimensional n>=2, 1<p<infinity and additive Euclidean regularization only; no infinite-dimensional/complex extension or exact bounded metric offset.
